cases.statement: MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n.name
MATCH (n:Person {name: 'Ada'}) WHERE n.age >= 18 RETURN n.name
MATCH (a:Person) OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[:KNOWS]->(b) RETURN a.name, b.name
MATCH (a:Person {name:'Ada'})-[:KNOWS*1..2]->(b) RETURN b.name
MATCH (n) RETURN n.label AS label, count(*) AS c
MATCH (n:Person) WITH n.age AS age WHERE age >= 40 RETURN age ORDER BY age
MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n.name AS x UNION ALL MATCH (m:City) RETURN m.name AS x
MATCH (n:Person {name:'Ada'}) RETURN toUpper(n.name)
MATCH (n:Person) RETURN CASE WHEN n.age >= 80 THEN 'senior' ELSE 'other' END
MATCH p = (:Person)-[:KNOWS]->(:Person) RETURN length(p)
cases.notes: Fixed-length path variables are supported; over variable-length they are not yet.

cases.statement: MATCH (n:Person {name: 'Ada'}) RETURN {name: n.name}['name'] AS m
MATCH (n) RETURN DISTINCT n.label AS l ORDER BY l
MATCH p = (:Person {name:'Ada'})-[:KNOWS]->(b) RETURN p
cases.notes: Path variables project as first-class Value::Path (Full39075 F6).

cases.statement: MATCH (a:Person)-[r:KNOWS]->(b) WITH collect(a) AS ns, collect(r) AS rs RETURN graph(ns, rs) AS g
cases.notes: graph(nodes, relationships) builds a deduplicated Value::Graph (Full39075 F7).

cases.statement: MATCH (a:Person)-[r:KNOWS]->(b) WITH collect(a) AS ns, collect(r) AS rs WITH graph(ns, rs) AS g RETURN size(nodes(g)) AS n, size(relationships(g)) AS r
MATCH (a:Person) CALL { MATCH (a)-[:KNOWS]->(b) RETURN b.name AS friend } RETURN a.name, friend
cases.notes: CALL { … } sees the outer row's bindings (correlated import-all scoping, Full39075 F8).

cases.statement: MATCH (n:Person) CALL { RETURN 1 AS one } RETURN n.name, one
cases.notes: Was the corpus's rejected `subquery-future` case before Full39075 F8 landed.

cases.statement: CALL { MATCH (p:Person {name:'Ada'}) RETURN p.name AS n UNION MATCH (c:City) RETURN c.name AS n } RETURN n ORDER BY n
MATCH (a:Person) CALL { MATCH (c:City) RETURN * } RETURN a.name
cases.notes: RETURN * inside CALL { … } would re-project the imported outer scope.

cases.statement: CALL tvf.range(1, 3) YIELD value RETURN value
cases.notes: TVF-style row source with argument expressions (Full39075 F9).

cases.statement: MATCH (n:Person {name:'Ada'}) CALL tvf.keys(n) YIELD key RETURN key ORDER BY key
cases.notes: TVF arguments are evaluated against each incoming row.

cases.statement: CALL db.labels('x') YIELD label RETURN label
cases.notes: The nullary db.* catalog procedures reject arguments with a structured type error.

cases.statement: CALL db.nope() YIELD x RETURN x
MATCH p = shortestPath((a:Person {name:'Ada'})-[:KNOWS*]->(b:Person {name:'Grace'})) RETURN length(p)
cases.notes: Minimal-length simple path per endpoint pair (Full39075 F10).

cases.statement: MATCH p = allShortestPaths((a:Person {name:'Ada'})-[:KNOWS*]->(b:Person)) RETURN b.name, length(p)
MATCH p = shortestPath((a)-[:KNOWS*]->(m)-[:KNOWS*]->(b)) RETURN p
cases.notes: shortestPath(…) covers exactly one relationship segment.

cases.statement: MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n.name, reduce(s = 0, x IN [n.age, 1] | s + x) AS total
cases.notes: A fold over any list expression; empty lists yield the seed and a NULL list yields NULL.

cases.statement: MATCH (n:Person) RETURN sum(reduce(s = 0, x IN [n.age, 1] | s + x)) AS total
cases.notes: The shape binding forms exist to express: a per-row fold inside an aggregate.

cases.statement: MATCH (n:Person) RETURN reduce(n = 0, x IN [1] | n + x)
cases.notes: A binding that shadows a row variable is an error, never resolved by precedence.

cases.statement: RETURN reduce(s = 0, x IN [1])
cases.notes: The syntax error names the form instead of a generic unclosed call.

cases.statement: MATCH (n:Person) RETURN [x IN [n.age, 1, 2] WHERE x > 1 | x * 2] AS xs
cases.notes: WHERE and the projection are each optional.

cases.statement: RETURN [x IN [1, 2] | [y IN [10, 20] WHERE y > x | x + y]] AS xs
cases.notes: Inner forms see outer bindings through the lexical scope.

cases.statement: RETURN [x IN [1, 2] | y]
MATCH (n:Person) WHERE any(x IN [n.age, 0] WHERE x % 2 = 0 AND x > 10) RETURN n.name
cases.notes: Arbitrary list expressions and predicates, not only item = value over a property.

cases.statement: RETURN all(x IN [1, 2] WHERE x > 0) AS a, none(x IN [1, 2] WHERE x > 5) AS n, single(x IN [1, 2] WHERE x = 1) AS s
MATCH (n:Person) RETURN any(n IN [1] WHERE n = 1)
